newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat export tax hinges on world prices - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat export tax hinges on world prices - ONIC.

text.p: The head of France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday that world price levels did not currently justify restoring a tax on European Union soft wheat exports although this could not be ruled out in the future if world prices were to head higher.
Alain Moulinier also said that technically the Commission could impose a tax on daily wheat exports at any time, if it wishes.
But to allow exporters to bid for taxes through the more rigid weekly grain auction channel, EU regulations would need to be changed and this was a lengthy process, he said.
"In any case at the moment we are not at the level (that would justify) a tax. World market prices are easing slightly. We will wait and see what happens," Moulinier told a news conference.

The European Union this week scrapped fixed daily refunds on wheat and flour, replacing them with a "nil" value entry in the face of soaring world prices. A nil value refund cannot be prefixed, leaving exporters subject to a tax, should the EU decide to impose one.
Grain traders said the move, which followed heavy bidding for wheat and flour this week in Europe, suggested the EU's 1996/97 export campaign was drawing to a close.
Moulinier said the EU's wheat export policy was driven mostly by the differential between domestic and world wheat prices, adding that the Commission could revert to taxes "at any time".
Michel Ferret, head of ONIC's international affairs division, said if it wished, the EU could technically decide to impose a tax on daily wheat exports on Thursday, with effect on Friday.
